document.title: Clean Air, Water Bodies, Environmental Accountability and Single-Use Plastic Prohibition Bill — claim provenance

claims.text: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 is a Central Act whose listed provisions include sections 21–24, 25–33B and 41–49.

authorities.title: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974

claims.subsequent_history_checked: India Code collection reviewed; every amendment and notification remains to be checked before introduction.
claims.limitations: This supports the existence and listed structure, not a final current-law opinion on every provision.
claims.reviewer_action: Verify official consolidated text and related notifications clause by clause.

claims.text: Section 24 of the Water Act prohibits specified use of a stream or well for disposal of polluting matter.

authorities.title: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, section 24
authorities.version_or_stage: current India Code section page retrieved 2026-08-09

claims.subsequent_history_checked: Not independently checked beyond the current India Code page.
claims.limitations: Exact scope and exceptions require full-text verification.
claims.reviewer_action: Check final wording and all amendments before cross-referencing.

claims.text: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is a Central Act whose listed provisions include central protective powers, hazardous-substance provisions, penalties, adjudication and appeals.
claims.subsequent_history_checked: India Code collection reviewed; penalty and delegated-law amendments remain to be checked.
claims.reviewer_action: Verify every consequential interaction and current provision.

claims.text: MoEFCC lists the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016 and amendments, and an official Ministry record describes a 2022 prohibition for identified low-utility, high-littering single-use plastic commodities.

authorities.title: MoEFCC Rules and Regulations
authorities.issuer: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

authorities.title: MoEFCC September 2021 record
authorities.issuer: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

claims.subsequent_history_checked: Later amendments are listed but not fully verified.
claims.limitations: Not a replacement for current Gazette consolidated text.
claims.reviewer_action: Retrieve every relevant Gazette amendment and current schedule.

claims.text: The Constitution contains Articles 14, 21, 48A, 51A(g), 245–254 and 253, which are relevant to equality, rights, environmental policy and legislative competence.
claims.subsequent_history_checked: Current text collection identified; exact competence analysis pending.
claims.limitations: This does not establish a final competence or constitutional-validity conclusion.
claims.reviewer_action: Obtain an independent public-law opinion on legislative entries and federal interaction.

claims.text: A new national-floor statute with a listed plastic ban, no-disposal rule, accountable public duties and due-process safeguards is a policy option.
claims.limitations: Requires technical, constitutional, fiscal and State/UT review.
claims.reviewer_action: Test against final research, consultation and specialist review.

claims.text: The Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2021 defined a single-use plastic commodity and prohibited the manufacture, import, stocking, distribution, sale and use of listed products from 1 July 2022, with a stated compostable-plastic qualification for a listed category.

authorities.title: Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2021, G.S.R. 571(E)
authorities.issuer: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change / Gazette of India

claims.subsequent_history_checked: The MoEFCC collection lists later amendments; their full interaction remains to be checked.
claims.limitations: The claim is limited to the 2021 notification text and is not a full current-consolidation opinion.
claims.reviewer_action: Verify later amendments before final consequential provisions.

claims.text: The National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 has provisions concerning tribunal disputes, relief, appellate jurisdiction, applications, procedure and enforcement.
claims.subsequent_history_checked: Current India Code collection reviewed; schedule interaction requires confirmation.
claims.limitations: Does not establish NGT jurisdiction for this proposed Act without further analysis.
claims.reviewer_action: Confirm Schedule I and jurisdiction before final drafting.

claims.text: Article 245(2) of the Constitution provides that a parliamentary law is not invalid merely because it has extra-territorial operation.
claims.limitations: It does not itself define a sufficient jurisdictional nexus or authorise coercive enforcement in another State's territory.
claims.reviewer_action: Obtain final public/international-law opinion on each extra-territorial enforcement route.

claims.text: UNCLOS Articles 192 and 194 provide for protection of the marine environment and measures concerning pollution from activities under a State's jurisdiction or control.

authorities.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, Part XII

claims.subsequent_history_checked: Treaty text reviewed; India-specific status and implementation route need confirmation.
claims.limitations: This does not establish domestic enforcement power beyond India's jurisdiction.
claims.reviewer_action: Verify India's treaty status and relevant maritime conventions before final filing.

claims.text: The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 defines air pollutant and air pollution and contains a structure for control areas, industrial consent, emission standards and restraint proceedings.

authorities.title: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981

claims.subsequent_history_checked: Current collection reviewed; current rules, standards, exemptions and State/UT application need further verification.
claims.limitations: This does not establish a final standard for every emission source.
claims.reviewer_action: Verify technical standards and consequential interaction before final filing.

claims.text: Article 20(1) of the Constitution prohibits conviction for an offence not in force when the act was committed and imposition of a greater penalty than then applicable.
claims.limitations: Application to a particular remedial order requires legal analysis; the Bill therefore separates prospective non-compliance from historic conduct.
claims.reviewer_action: Review every legacy-pollution clause for punitive substance and operation.

claims.text: The Constitution protects legislators from court proceedings solely for speech or a vote in Parliament or a State Legislature, and provides constitutional routes for membership disqualification decisions.
claims.limitations: The scope of privilege and the exact electoral consequence of a proposed conviction require final constitutional and election-law review.
claims.reviewer_action: Ensure the Bill does not itself remove/disqualify a legislator or criminalise protected speech/voting alone.

claims.text: The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 has provisions on anti-corruption offences, special judges, investigation, official-decision approval, prosecution sanction, attachment and appeal.

authorities.title: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
authorities.version_or_stage: current India Code collection and official PDF retrieved 2026-08-10

claims.subsequent_history_checked: Official India Code collection and PDF retrieved; application to any particular allegation needs legal analysis.
claims.limitations: The Bill must not use a differently labelled offence to evade mandatory procedure that applies to a corruption allegation.
claims.reviewer_action: Map each overlap before final filing and identify the proper court, investigator, sanction/approval route and attachment process.

claims.text: Article 368 supplies the constitutional-amendment procedure, including the specified special-majority requirement in each House; an ordinary Bill does not itself amend Part III of the Constitution.
claims.limitations: Whether a particular amendment needs State ratification and complies with the basic structure requires a complete constitutional analysis.
claims.reviewer_action: Do not describe the proposed Article 21B as enacted or introduction-ready without Article 368 and constitutional review.

claims.text: Sections 4 and 5 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 apply its procedure to offences under other laws subject to a special enactment regulating the manner or place of investigation, inquiry or trial, and preserve special procedure unless specifically displaced.
claims.limitations: This supports a proposed special-procedure schedule; every interaction with the First Schedule and coercive powers still needs parliamentary criminal-procedure review.
claims.reviewer_action: Verify offence classification, court, cognizance, bail and safeguards against the final parliamentary draft.

claims.text: BIS materials identify IS 10500:2012, Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision), as reviewed in 2023, and describe IS 19757:2026 as guidance for alternative drinking-water service during crisis.
claims.limitations: These sources do not decide local quantity, access-time, ecological-flow or contaminant thresholds.
claims.reviewer_action: Use the referenced standards as a floor and obtain independent public-health, accessibility, hydrology and laboratory review before setting local numerical values.
